name: Kwame Nkrumah
position: Prime Minister and President of Ghana
biography: Kwame Nkrumah was a Ghanaian nationalist leader who played a major role in Ghana's independence movement and became one of the leading voices for Pan-African unity.
achievements: Supported African political and economic unity
timeline: 1947: Returned to the Gold Coast and became involved in nationalist politics
1966: Nkrumah was overthrown in a military coup
quote: Freedom is not something that one people can bestow on another as a gift.

name: Thomas Sankara
biography: Thomas Sankara was a revolutionary leader who introduced ambitious reforms focused on national self-reliance, social equality, health, education, and women's rights.
quote: We must dare to invent the future.

name: Steve Biko
biography: Steve Biko was a South African anti-apartheid activist and a leading figure in the Black Consciousness Movement.
achievements: Founded the South African Students' Organisation
timeline: 1968: Helped establish the South African Students' Organisation
1972: Became involved with Black Community Programmes
1973: Was banned by the apartheid government
1977: Was detained and died in police custody
quote: The most potent weapon in the hands of the oppressor is the mind of the oppressed.

name: Patrice Lumumba
position: First Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
biography: Patrice Lumumba was a Congolese independence leader who became the country's first prime minister after independence from Belgium.
achievements: Helped lead the Congolese independence movement
Became the first Prime Minister of independent Congo
timeline: 1958: Helped establish the Congolese National Movement
quote: The history of Africa will be written in Africa itself.

name: Julius Nyerere
biography: Julius Nyerere was a Tanzanian nationalist leader and the country's first president who promoted African socialism and national unity.
timeline: 1954: Helped establish the Tanganyika African National Union
1964: Tanganyika and Zanzibar united to form Tanzania
quote: Unity will not make us rich, but it can make it difficult for Africa to be disregarded.

name: Ahmed Sékou Touré
biography: Ahmed Sékou Touré was a Guinean nationalist leader who led Guinea to independence from France in 1958.
timeline: 1956: Became a leading figure in Guinean politics
quote: We prefer poverty in liberty to riches in slavery.

name: Haile Selassie
biography: Haile Selassie was Ethiopia's emperor and an influential figure in African diplomacy and the development of continental cooperation.
achievements: Supported the creation of the Organization of African Unity
timeline: 1963: Hosted the founding conference of the Organization of African Unity
quote: Throughout history, it has been the inaction of those who could have acted.
